transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Rourke (Redwood) — Sara Patel, Arjun Rao, Melanie Cruz, Tom Becker (HelixHealth)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay great, thanks everyone for joining on time. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Liam on the SE side. Quick round of intros?
[00:12] Sara Patel: Hi Sara here, Director of ML. Arjun is our SRE, Melanie product, Tom security.
[00:18] Liam O'Rourke: Hey all. Quick agenda: run through the cutover plan, define canary size and metrics, A/B plan if we need it, monitoring and alerting, then runbooks and final owner signoffs.
[00:30] Arjun Rao: Sounds good. We have a hard constraint — no customer-facing downtime between 02:00-06:00 PST next week due to regional maintenance, so we need to lock window.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Noted. Proposed cutover window we suggested last week was 03:00-04:30 to minimize overlap with peak. Is that still workable?
[00:50] Sara Patel: 03:00-04:30 is fine for the core team; I'll confirm with ops but seems acceptable.
[01:02] Melanie Cruz: Quick Q on customer segmentation: for the canary, do we want a specific cohort? Small percentage of new users or synthetic traffic?
[01:15] Liam O'Rourke: We recommend a hybrid: start with synthetic traffic that mirrors peak request distribution to validate latency/cost and KV cache warmup, then switch to 1% of production user sessions for behavioral checks. Synthetic first avoids early user impact.
[01:30] Tom Becker: From security we need to ensure any synthetic traffic doesn't hit PII-sensitive endpoints. Also KMS key access must be scoped to the staging nodes.
[01:45] Maya Chen: We'll include a step in the runbook to route synthetic traffic to a scrubbed dataset. Also list the KMS principal that will be used. Liam, can you add that?
[01:55] Liam O'Rourke: Yep, will add KMS principal and scrubbing step to the runbook.
[02:08] Sara Patel: Can we define canary success criteria right now? Latency SLOs, error rates, token cost anomaly thresholds?
[02:20] Liam O'Rourke: Proposed canary pass conditions: 95th percentile latency within 15% of baseline, error rate < 0.5% on user-facing endpoints, token cost per request within +/- 10% of observed POC baseline, and no increase in tail latency over 200ms. Also KV cache hit rate above 70% after synthetic warmup.
[02:42] Arjun Rao: For monitoring, we want alerts for both latency regressions and cost spikes. Can Redwood emit a per-route token breakdown to our Datadog?
[02:55] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route; we can push metrics to Datadog via our exporter. Liam, is there an existing integration doc?
[03:05] Liam O'Rourke: I'll share the Datadog integration steps. We recommend dashboard widgets: per-route TPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token cost per minute, KV cache hit rate. Also add a synthetic heartbeat monitor.
[03:20] Melanie Cruz: For the A/B plan, if we want to test an experience change alongside model variant, what's the simplest approach?
[03:30] Liam O'Rourke: We can do an A/B by routing 20% to model variant B and 80% to baseline using Redwood routing policies. Keep the payload identical and compare quality metrics from your eval set; disable sampling for deterministic comparisons. Use canary first for stability then A/B for product metrics.
[03:48] Sara Patel: How fast can we ramp traffic? We don't want to overload the dedicated pool.
[03:55] Liam O'Rourke: Recommend geometric ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%, with 15-30 minute observation windows depending on traffic. If SLA/burst capacity is available we can be more aggressive but default is cautious.
[04:15] Arjun Rao: That ramp fits our capacity planning. For rollback — what triggers an automatic rollback in Redwood?
[04:23] Maya Chen: You can configure automatic fallback policies: if the model variant exceeds set thresholds (error rate, tail latency, cost anomaly), Redwood will automatically route back to a healthy model. We'll include the exact configuration snippets in the runbook.
[04:35] Tom Becker: About auditing — we need the audit logs for every rollout action and model switch. Is that captured?
[04:43] Liam O'Rourke: Yes, Private and Dedicated both emit audit logs; hosted has an audit trail in the console. We can forward logs to your SIEM. We'll include log retention and KMS encryption notes in the security checklist.
[04:58] Melanie Cruz: Do we have a recommended post-cutover validation checklist? Quick sanity tests we should run within the first hour?
[05:06] Maya Chen: Yes — health endpoints, spike tests at 10% traffic, basic throughput checks, sample a small set of user queries and run the eval harness to compare outputs, then monitor metrics for 4 hours. We'll add an ordered checklist in the runbook.
[05:22] Sara Patel: On the runbook timeline — when do you expect to share the draft?
[05:27] Liam O'Rourke: I can share a first draft and the traffic ramp script by Thursday, 2025-10-23. It will include YAML snippets for routing policies and the Datadog dashboards.
[05:38] Arjun Rao: We'll run a rehearsal in staging. How do we best simulate KV cache warmup?
[05:45] Liam O'Rourke: Use the synthetic generator to replay representative sessions for 60 minutes prior to canary start to warm KV and embeddings caches. The script we'll share includes timings and request distribution.
[05:58] Tom Becker: A note on SAML/SSO — for the cutover we need console access locked down to the on-call list. Can we temporarily restrict admin roles?
[06:07] Maya Chen: Yes you can configure RBAC to a minimal admin group and then expand post-cutover. We'll document a step: limit console access to cutover-admins and ensure MFA.
[06:20] Melanie Cruz: If the canary shows a model quality regression but metrics are within SLOs, do we keep running?
[06:29] Liam O'Rourke: That's a product call. We recommend automated guardrails for infra signals (latency/cost/errors), and manual hold for quality regressions. In the runbook we'll add a manual quality gate where product/ML review is required before full ramp.
[06:45] Sara Patel: Good — we want that manual hold. Also, can Redwood provide a feature to snapshot model outputs for forensic analysis?
[06:53] Maya Chen: Redwood can persist structured output and we have structured output support; we'll include how to export samples to your S3 bucket with redaction options.
[07:05] Arjun Rao: Let's talk about rollbacks: if we revert, how long until traffic is stable? What's the expected state?
[07:13] Liam O'Rourke: Rollback is immediate at routing layer; traffic flips back within seconds. But KV cold start may cause a latency transient for a few minutes as caches refill — we call that warmup window. Plan for a 10-15 minute watch after rollback.
[07:30] Tom Becker: For compliance we need the canary decision and the final rollout documented as part of audit. Will Redwood provide an artefact?
[07:38] Maya Chen: Yes, after the cutover we'll provide a post-mortem package with timings, metric deltas, and the audit log snippet.
[07:48] Melanie Cruz: Anything else on A/B? If we see small quality wins but cost increases, how do we instrument per-user cost attribution?
[07:57] Liam O'Rourke: Use per-route token accounting and tag requests with user cohort metadata; Redwood console exports token-level cost per route so you can map cohorts to cost. We'll include a sample dashboard.
[08:15] Sara Patel: Ok, let's confirm owners and dates for the key artifacts — runbook draft from Redwood by 10/23, security checklist answers from Tom by 10/24, staging dry-run and traffic tests by 10/24, rehearsal week of 10/27.
[08:30] Maya Chen: I'll summarize in the email and update the runbook link when Liam posts it.
[08:38] Arjun Rao: Minor thing — we need to ensure the traffic generator can hit multiple regions to validate routing policies.
[08:45] Liam O'Rourke: We'll include a multi-region test plan.
[08:50] Melanie Cruz: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:53] Maya Chen: None — Liam has the action to publish the runbook. We'll also provide the Datadog integration doc and a sample YAML for automated fallback.
[09:02] Sara Patel: Good, thanks. Tom, any security items to add?
[09:07] Tom Becker: We need confirmation on KMS rotation windows and whether Redwood's logs will include de-identified request IDs — I'll follow up in the checklist.
[09:16] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include KMS rotation guidance in the security checklist.
[09:22] Melanie Cruz: When do we meet next? Weekly same time?
[09:25] Sara Patel: Weekly until cutover, yes. Same time next Tuesday?
[09:29] Maya Chen: I'll send calendar invite for 2025-10-28 15:00 UTC.
[09:33] Liam O'Rourke: I'll upload the runbook to the shared drive and post link in Slack.
[09:38] Maya Chen: Excellent. Recap of action items and owners are in the follow-up email. Thanks everyone.
[09:45] Meeting end.
